text:
Colton Dach, a Fort Saskatchewan native playing for the team just down the road, has found a scoring touch in the Oilers' bottom six. He had Edmonton's only goal in a 3-1 loss at Tampa Bay on Nov. 19, then scored again in St. Louis three nights later. That makes 5 goals in 20 games on about 14 minutes a night, 4 of them in his last ten.

The finishing is a little ahead of the chances (5 goals on 3.5 expected), but not wildly, and his 15% shooting sits inside his normal range. The bigger problem is everything else at five on five: Edmonton has taken just 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than eight points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern last season, his team creating little when he was out there, partly because his linemates were weak. He uses his 6'3" frame (48 hits), and our numbers project about 15 goals. What we'd watch is whether his line can spend more of its shifts in the other end.
headline: Colton Dach finds the net close to home
